description: CAREYONDA is an innovative Astronaut Health Monitoring System designed to monitor astronauts' vital signs and overall health during space missions. The project aims to combine healthcare, AI, and space technology to support astronaut safety through real-time monitoring, intelligent health analysis, and early risk detection. We are looking for passionate teammates with skills in Biomedical Engineering, AI & Data Science, Embedded Systems, and Software Development to help bring this idea to life.
summary:
CAREYONDA: evidence-first health and environment monitoring for long-duration spaceflight

CAREYONDA is an offline-first research platform that brings astronaut health observations and spacecraft environmental data together in one explainable decision-support workspace.
details:
What CAREYONDA does

CAREYONDA is an offline-first research platform for astronaut health and spaceflight environmental hazards. It collects health and habitat observations into one validated evidence format. It then runs explainable analyses and shows the results in a dashboard, where every conclusion links back to the measurements behind it.

How it works

  1. Evidence layer. Every measurement becomes a versioned observation that records its value, unit, timestamp, source, quality and origin (measured, self-reported, derived or simulated). Missing and unavailable readings are stored explicitly, never replaced with zeros.
  2. Data sources:
    • a seeded mission simulator for synthetic crew data;
    • a pipeline for real NASA OSDR Rodent Research-1 ISS cabin telemetry (CO₂, temperature, humidity), split by time into training, validation and test periods.
  3. Analysis components:
    • Model A: an unsupervised Isolation Forest that ranks unusual NASA cabin-environment readings.
    • Model B: anomaly detection on synthetic multi-signal health data.
    • Model C: a deterministic sleep/fatigue monitor that compares each person only with their own earlier history.
    • M2: a rule-based reasoner that ranks possible explanations (elevated CO₂, sleep deprivation, recent exercise) and lists supporting, contradicting and missing evidence.
  4. Interface: a React dashboard backed by a FastAPI service, covering health, environment, the data explorer, AI findings, incident review and the Model C self-report flow.

Benefits and intended impact

  • Crew autonomy. On long missions with delayed communication, crews need tools that connect how they feel with the environment they live in.
  • Trust through transparency. Results show their evidence, uncertainty and limitations. When data is too thin, the system abstains instead of guessing.
  • Research foundation. Versioned contracts and reproducible pipelines let future models be added and compared fairly.

CAREYONDA is research decision support. It does not diagnose, prescribe or control spacecraft.

Tools and technologies

  • Backend: Python 3.12, Pydantic v2, FastAPI, Uvicorn, scikit-learn, NumPy, joblib.
  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Zod, Recharts, Tailwind CSS.
  • Quality:
    • Python: pytest (500+ backend tests), Ruff, strict mypy;
    • frontend: Vitest, Testing Library, Prettier.
  • Data: NASA OSDR Environmental Data App (RR-1), plus synthetic datasets.
  • Workflow: Git and GitHub, with AI coding assistants for implementation and review.
  • Hardware: standard Windows laptops. No special hardware is required, and the system runs fully offline.
  • Planned: a Supabase (PostgreSQL) design with role-based access for Admin, Doctor and Astronaut users. It is designed and documented, not yet implemented.

What makes it creative

  • Abstention is a real result. "Not enough evidence" is shown clearly, with reasons, instead of a forced score.
  • Personal baselines. Model C compares a person only with their own history, not with a population average.
  • Honest provenance. Self-reports are kept distinct from sensor data, real data is never mixed with synthetic, and NASA environmental readings are never presented as one astronaut's health data.
  • Full evidence trails. Every finding links back to the exact observations behind it.

Factors the team considered

  • Safety: no invented clinical thresholds, no probabilities presented as health risk, and no autonomous actions.
  • Data integrity: explicit handling of missing data, consistent UTC timestamps, explicit units (CO₂ in ppm is never confused with partial pressure in Pa), and no test-set leakage.
  • Data rights: the NASA-derived data is kept local until redistribution rights are confirmed.
  • Privacy: pseudonymous participant IDs, synthetic data during development, and no data stored in the browser.
  • Reliability and accessibility: works offline, reproducible builds, keyboard support and reduced-motion support.
projectRefs: Temperature, humidity and CO₂ measurements from ISS-related missions
